:::{#exm-composition}
#### The order of composition matters

Let $g : \reals \to \reals$ with $g(x) = x + 1$,
and $f : \reals \to \reals$ with $f(x) = x^2$.

- $$
  \begin{aligned}
  (f \circ g)(2) &= f(g(2)) \\
  &= f(3) \\
  &= 9:
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  $g$ is the inner function, and $f$ is the outer function.
- $$
  \begin{aligned}
  (g \circ f)(2) &= g(f(2)) \\
  &= g(4) \\
  &= 5:
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  now $f$ is the inner function, and $g$ is the outer function.

Since $9 \ne 5$, $f \circ g$ and $g \circ f$ are different functions.

:::
